title: Ransomware Incident Response and Containment Playbook
source: CISA / MS-ISAC StopRansomware Guide & NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2
content:
### 1. OVERVIEW & DETECTION
Ransomware attacks involve unauthorized encryption of file systems, databases, or virtual machines, often accompanied by data exfiltration (double extortion) and volume shadow copy deletion. Early detection indicators include:
- Mass file renaming or rapid creation of files with unfamiliar extensions (e.g., .locked, .crypto, .enc).
- Execution of volume shadow copy deletion commands (e.g., vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet, wbadmin delete catalog -quiet, bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No).
- Unauthorized termination or disabling of security agents, endpoint protection services, or database engines.
- Ransom note drops in multiple directories (e.g., README_FOR_DECRYPT.txt, HOW_TO_RESTORE_FILES.html).

### 2. EVIDENCE & ARTIFACTS TO EXAMINE
- Endpoint Event Logs: Windows Security Event ID 4688 (Process Creation with Command Line), Sysmon Event ID 1 (Process Create), Sysmon Event ID 11 (File Create for mass file modifications), Sysmon Event ID 7 (Image Loaded for injected DLLs).
- Volume Shadow Status: Execute vssadmin list shadows to assess if shadow copies remain intact.
- Network Connection Logs: Outbound connections to unknown external IPs or TOR exit nodes indicative of Command and Control (C2) beaconing or active data exfiltration.
- Active Directory & Authentication: Windows Event ID 4624 (Logon Type 3 / Network or Type 10 / RemoteInteractive), Event ID 4720 (Account Creation), and Event ID 4728/4732 (Group Membership Changes) reflecting privileged account escalation or lateral movement.

### 3. INVESTIGATION & TRIAGE
- Determine Scope: Identify the initial infection vector (phishing email, exposed RDP, vulnerable public-facing web service, compromised VPN credentials).
- Process Inspection: Trace parent-child process relationships for suspicious parent binaries (e.g., powershell.exe, cmd.exe, wscript.exe, rundll32.exe spawning cipher utilities or network scanners).
- Persistence Mechanisms: Inspect scheduled tasks (schtasks.exe), registry run keys (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run), WMI event subscriptions, and newly created local administrative accounts.

### 4. CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES
- Immediate Network Isolation: Disconnect infected and suspicious endpoints from local networks, Wi-Fi, and VPNs immediately. If remote management isolation is available through EDR, apply host isolation without shutting down the host.
- Preserve Volatile Memory: Do NOT immediately reboot or power off the machine if live forensic memory capture is possible, as encryption keys, injected processes, and active network connections reside in RAM.
- Active Directory Quarantine: Disable or force password resets for all compromised domain and local accounts involved in the incident. Invalidate active Kerberos Golden/Silver tickets by resetting the KRBTGT password twice if domain compromise is suspected.
- Segment Storage & Backups: Immediately sever network access to backup storage repositories and verify offline/immutable backup integrity to prevent ransomware from encrypting recovery media.

### 5. ERADICATION, RECOVERY & REMEDIATION
- Root Cause Eradication: Patch the vulnerability or remediate the compromised credential vector that allowed initial access.
- Clean Rebuild: Rebuild infected systems from known-good base images rather than attempting partial malware removal on encrypted operating systems.
- Backup Restoration: Restore critical business data from verified immutable or offline backups taken prior to the initial compromise timestamp.
- Post-Incident Monitoring: Maintain heightened SOC telemetry monitoring and egress traffic inspection on all restored assets for at least 30 days.
